This implementation isn't wrong at all, but keep in mind that all floating point literals are already of type `double` like default, so there's no need to cast it to type `double`.

Also keep in mind that explicitly casting a literal's own type doesn't have any effect on `catch` behavior. While C++ would normally coerce, for example, a `double` to an `int` if a `double` was passed as an argument into a function taking an `int`, this *is not* the case for `catch` statements. Exception handlers will not coerce or cast the thrown type in C++, at least as far as the reading described.
